S1.hook: Tested on the faces walking out.
S1.dek: The Department of Homeland Security Science and Technology Directorate ran it for Customs and Border Protection at the Progreso International Bridge in Hidalgo County. The bridge director puts the annual walk out at over 1.1 million.

S2.hook: It had to account for hats and umbrellas.
S2.dek: Customs and Border Protection asked for it in October 2025. Cameras went up on poles at different heights, so people of different statures would land in frame. The technologies had to account for walking pace, hats, sunglasses and umbrellas.

S3.hook: Six were invited. Three came south.
S3.dek: Six companies were invited to the Maryland Test Facility. Three solutions were carried forward for data collection at the bridge.

S4.dek: A replica of the pedestrian exit environment went up at the Maryland Test Facility first, so the vendors could install and assess their prototypes before taking them to the crossing.

S5.dek: Artificial intelligence and other technologies built a three dimensional model of the capture zone, watched pedestrian movement, and judged whether a face was good enough to match in Customs and Border Protection's Traveler Verification Service. The account gives no rate for how often it was right.

S6.hook: One lane was provided for saying no.
S6.dek: Signs in English and Spanish told pedestrians that United States citizens could opt out. An opt-out lane was provided. The mandate the test serves applies to travelers who are not citizens.

S7.hook: The way in is counted every month.
S7.dek: 101,306 pedestrians entered the United States here in May 2026, the month the partners were at the bridge. No comparable data is collected on the way out.

S8.hook: Eight slots. Three of them filled.
S8.dek: Two agencies and one vendor filed a finding. Five measurements were never stated rather than removed.

S9.hook: The only date belongs to Dallas.
S9.dek: The account announces no comment period, no hearing and no docket. The nearest dated room in this record is a different program. Dallas takes a briefing on its police Flock plate readers on September 8th, 2026.
